summary: ZestButton gets an optional toggle mode, like a Bold button in an editor: it stays pressed when on and returns to normal when off. When on it shows a pressed look plus a small animated check mark; the check mark can sit at the start or end of the button so icons still work. Screen readers hear 'pressed' instead of the check mark. It is additive: buttons that do not turn it on look and behave exactly as before. It is for developers who install the library and for the people who use their apps.
roles: Developer: installs the library and turns on toggle mode with props
App user: clicks, taps or uses the keyboard on the toggle and must always be able to tell whether it is on or off
Screen-reader user: hears whether the toggle is pressed

requirements.text: A developer can turn a ZestButton into a toggle through a new optional `zest.toggleOptions` prop. Without it the button renders and behaves exactly as it does today.
requirements.rationale: The builder decided the on/off state is a mode of ZestButton, not a separate control. Existing apps must not change on update.
acceptance: <ZestButton zest={{ toggleOptions: {} }}>Bold</ZestButton> renders a button that exposes a pressed state (aria-pressed='false' when off)
A ZestButton without toggleOptions has no aria-pressed attribute and its existing tests still pass unchanged
The toggleOptions type is exported from UI/index.ts and the change is recorded as additive, with no breaking change
edgeCases: toggleOptions set to an empty object still enables toggle mode (off by default)
Removing toggleOptions on a later render returns the button to a plain button with no aria-pressed
pitfalls: Existing props, defaults and rendered markup of non-toggle buttons must not change
A removed or renamed export would be breaking and must not happen

requirements.text: The on/off value can be controlled by the app (`pressed` plus `onPressedChange`) or left to the button (`defaultPressed`, off when not given). Each click or key press on an enabled toggle calls onPressedChange with the new value.
requirements.rationale: Apps like editor toolbars keep the value in their own state; simple uses just want it to work. Supporting both is the usual pattern for toggles.
acceptance: With defaultPressed omitted the toggle starts off; one click turns it on and onPressedChange(true) is called once; a second click turns it off and calls onPressedChange(false)
With pressed={true} the toggle shows on; clicking calls onPressedChange(false) and the button only changes when the app passes pressed={false}
defaultPressed={true} starts the toggle on
The existing onClick handler is still called on each click, in addition to onPressedChange
edgeCases: If the app keeps pressed fixed and ignores onPressedChange, the button keeps showing that fixed value
Two rapid clicks flip the value twice, once per click; they are not merged or lost
If both pressed and defaultPressed are given, pressed wins
pitfalls: The visual state and aria-pressed must never disagree
A controlled toggle must not flip on its own before the app updates the value

facts.subject: toggle
facts.attribute: initial state when no value given

requirements.text: When on, the button shows a pressed look (tinted or filled background with inset shading) plus a small check mark that animates in; when off, it shows the normal look with no check mark, and the check animates out when turning off.
requirements.rationale: Builder decision: pressed look plus check mark, so on is clear even to people who cannot tell colours apart, and it renders beautifully.
acceptance: On shows a visible check mark and the pressed look; off shows neither
Turning on or off plays a short animation of the check mark; the button's outer size does not jump when it appears
The check mark is hidden from screen readers (aria-hidden) and the button exposes aria-pressed='true' instead
The on look works with every existing variant, buttonStyle (solid, outline, text, dashed) and size, and is visibly different from off in each
edgeCases: A text-only or very long label does not overlap, clip or push out the check mark; the label wraps or truncates as it does today
Dashed and outline styles show on clearly even though they have no fill when off
When the user has asked for reduced motion, the check mark and pressed look change without animation
pitfalls: Colour alone must not be the only difference between on and off
The check mark must not be confused with the existing success checkmark shown after an async action

requirements.text: The developer can choose whether the check mark sits at the start or the end of the button with `toggleOptions.checkPosition` ('start' or 'end'). Existing iconLeft and iconRight keep rendering alongside it.
requirements.rationale: Builder decision: the position is configurable so buttons that already use icons are still supported.
acceptance: checkPosition='start' places the check mark before the label; 'end' places it after the label
With iconLeft and checkPosition='start', both the icon and the check mark are visible and neither overlaps the other
With iconRight and checkPosition='end', both are visible without overlap
When checkPosition is not given the check mark appears at the start
edgeCases: An unknown checkPosition value falls back to the default instead of hiding the check mark
In a right-to-left page, start and end follow the page direction
With stretch (full width) the check mark stays next to the label
pitfalls: Adding the check mark must not remove or reorder the developer's own icons

requirements.text: The toggle is fully operable by keyboard and assistive technology: it is focusable, Space and Enter toggle it, it shows a visible focus ring in both states, and it exposes aria-pressed with the current value.
requirements.rationale: UI-001 requires keyboard use and correct ARIA. A toggle that screen readers cannot read as pressed or not pressed fails its purpose.
acceptance: Pressing Space or Enter on a focused toggle flips it once
aria-pressed is 'true' when on and 'false' when off, and updates on every change
A visible focus indicator appears on keyboard focus whether the toggle is on or off
The touch target is at least as large as the existing button for its size setting
edgeCases: Holding the key down does not flip the toggle repeatedly
A toggle with only an icon and no text still exposes on/off state; the developer supplies the aria-label
pitfalls: The button's role must not change (no role='switch'); it stays a button that reports pressed

requirements.text: The toggle looks right in light, dark and system themes, using the same theme variables as the rest of the button, and sizes everything in rem (px only for borders).
requirements.rationale: UI-001 and the library's existing theming; on must stay readable and distinct in every theme.
acceptance: In light, dark and system themes, on is visibly distinct from off and the label and check mark are as readable as the existing button text
The new styles use CSS variables and rem units; no px except borders
The change adds no new font, image, dependency or runtime asset; the check mark reuses the check shape the button already has
edgeCases: Hover and active states on an on toggle are still distinguishable from the plain on state
With the system theme, the toggle follows the OS setting changing while it is on
pitfalls: Growing the bundle noticeably or adding a new dependency for the check mark

requirements.text: A toggle works together with the existing button features: while disabled or busy it does not flip and shows its current state; with a confirmation it flips only after the user confirms; with a dropdown the main part toggles and the dropdown arrow behaves as before.
requirements.rationale: The toggle lives on ZestButton, so a developer will combine it with these options and must not get surprises.
acceptance: A disabled toggle ignores clicks and keyboard, and still shows on or off clearly (dimmed like any disabled button)
While busy (async onClick), clicks do not flip the toggle and the busy spinner shows as today
With confirmOptions, the first click shows the confirm label and does not flip; the confirming click flips once; letting the confirm time out leaves the state unchanged
With dropdownOptions, clicking the main part toggles; opening the dropdown does not change the state
edgeCases: If onClick throws or rejects, the toggle keeps the value it flipped to (the app can correct it by controlling `pressed`)
A semanticType combined with toggle mode keeps its icon and label defaults, and the on look is still shown
pitfalls: Double clicks during busy or confirm must not flip the state twice or skip the confirmation

requirements.text: Toggle mode is documented where readers look: a first working example in README.md, recipes, the feature description, the new props and the 'additive, not breaking' note in the documentation pages.
requirements.rationale: DOC-001: a feature nobody can find does not get used, and the library ships its documentation.
acceptance: README.md shows a working toggle example (for example a Bold button with defaultPressed and onPressedChange)
documentation/examples.md has recipes for controlled, uncontrolled, check at the end with an icon, and toggle with confirmation
documentation/features.md describes the pressed look, check mark and accessibility behaviour
documentation/api.md lists pressed, defaultPressed, onPressedChange and checkPosition with types and defaults
documentation/configuration.md and documentation/breaking-changes.md mention toggle mode (breaking-changes states it is not breaking), and each page links to the previous and next page
edgeCases: Every code example in the docs compiles against the exported types
pitfalls: Docs that describe props the code does not have or omit ones it does

requirements.text: Tests prove that existing ZestButton behaviour is unchanged and that every toggle requirement above holds.
requirements.rationale: USR-004: ZestButton is already merged and published, so its current behaviour is pinned by tests before it is extended.
acceptance: Characterization tests for the existing click, busy, success, confirm, dropdown and rendering behaviour pass before and after the change
New tests cover on and off rendering, aria-pressed, controlled and uncontrolled use, check position, keyboard, disabled, busy and confirm interplay
The full test suite passes
edgeCases: Tests check the resulting state, not animation timing
pitfalls: Editing existing test expectations to make the new feature pass

outOfScope: A separate switch control with a sliding track and knob
Grouping toggles into radio-like or exclusive toggle groups
Custom on and off icons other than the check mark (developers can still use iconLeft and iconRight)
Remembering the on/off value between page loads
Changing the look or behaviour of buttons that do not turn on toggle mode

nonFunctional.statement: State is conveyed by shape and aria-pressed as well as colour; the focus ring is visible; reduced-motion preferences are honoured.
nonFunctional.acceptance: Tests assert aria-pressed, aria-hidden on the check mark and the check mark's presence only when on; a reduced-motion style rule exists for the new animations.

nonFunctional.statement: Toggling re-renders only the toggle button, leaves no timers or listeners running after unmount, and adds no new dependency or asset to the bundle.
nonFunctional.acceptance: Review of the diff shows no new dependency, listener or timer left running after unmount; the build still produces the same set of output files.

nonFunctional.statement: Works in light, dark and system themes, on small screens first, in Next.js App Router apps and in apps on React 18 and 19.
nonFunctional.acceptance: Existing build-externalization and peer-dependency tests still pass; the component stays usable from client components as it is today.

risks: Rendered markup of non-toggle buttons must stay identical because apps may style against it.
The existing success checkmark and the new on-state check mark could look alike; they must stay distinguishable in context.
glossary: Toggle: a button that stays pressed (on) until pressed again (off).
Pressed look: the tinted or filled, inset appearance that shows the toggle is on.
Controlled toggle: the app owns the on/off value and passes it in as `pressed`.
Uncontrolled toggle: the button keeps the value itself, starting from `defaultPressed`.

coverage.note: Developers installing the library and their app users; decided: a toggle mode on ZestButton.
No stored data. The on/off value is held by the app (pressed) or by the button (defaultPressed); both supported (R2).
A UI library with no records, sign-in or ownership.
Unknown checkPosition falls back to start; toggle with confirm, busy, disabled and dropdown defined in R7.
Builder chose pressed look plus a check mark, position configurable start or end (R3, R4); disabled and busy covered in R7.
One flip per click; no flips while busy, disabled or awaiting confirmation (R2, R7).
A single control; no lists, paging or searching.
No personal data is collected or kept.
Light/dark/system themes, keyboard, aria-pressed, rem sizing, React 18 and 19, additive change, docs (R5, R6, R8, nonFunctional).

assumptions: The toggle is additive: it is off unless the developer passes zest.toggleOptions, so existing buttons are unchanged.
Both app-controlled (pressed) and self-managed (defaultPressed) use are supported; pressed wins if both are given.
The check mark defaults to the start of the button when checkPosition is not given.
If onClick fails, the toggle keeps its flipped value; apps that need otherwise control `pressed`.
